chosen.premise: Seel hunts beneath ice, then uses its head horn to punch a breathing hole when it needs air.
chosen.hook: Seel's horn isn't just a weapon—it's an emergency snorkel.
chosen.visualIdea: Animate Seel hunting under an ice sheet, then drilling upward with its horn to create an air hole.
chosen.note: A highly Seel-specific survival mechanic with a clear visual sequence. “Emergency snorkel” is a strong metaphor, though the Pokédex only explicitly says it punches a breathing hole.

candidates.premise: Seel thrives in water around 14°F and remains active even at -40°F.
candidates.hook: For Seel, temperatures that hurt us are basically a spa day.
candidates.visualIdea: Show a thermometer dropping from 14°F to -40°F while Seel becomes increasingly cheerful.
candidates.note: The 14°F and -40°F figures create a strong, immediately visual temperature escalation. It is distinctive to Seel, though the basic cold-resistance premise could fit several Ice-associated Pokémon.

candidates.premise: Thick fat protects Seel from cold seas, but warm water makes it tire easily.
candidates.hook: Seel's superpower against cold becomes useless in warm water.
candidates.visualIdea: Transition from energetic Seel in icy water to exhausted Seel as the water visibly warms.
candidates.note: The reversal is concrete and interesting: cold helps Seel while warm water tires it. The hook slightly overstates this as a superpower becoming useless, but the cited entry supports the core claim.

candidates.premise: Seel was believed to live only in cold seas, so its appearance in Alola is officially called a mystery.
candidates.hook: Seel showing up in Alola breaks what people thought they knew about it.
candidates.visualIdea: Build a frozen habitat map, then place a question mark over Alola as Seel suddenly appears there.
candidates.note: The contradiction between Seel’s supposed cold-sea habitat and its Alola appearance is genuinely intriguing. It is more of a setup for a mystery than a resolved payoff, and the research does not explain why it happens.

candidates.premise: At level 34, Seel evolves into Dewgong and gains the Ice type alongside Water.
candidates.hook: Seel's cold obsession becomes official at level 34.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Seel leveling from 33 to 34, transforming into Dewgong as an Ice-type label appears.
candidates.note: Very concrete and highly visual, but evolution-at-a-level is a familiar Pokémon format and the evolution method/type details rely partly on trusted secondary data rather than the Pokédex entries.

candidates.premise: Seel struggles to walk on land but is described as a graceful swimmer in frigid seas.
candidates.hook: Seel looks clumsy—until it gets into the water.
candidates.visualIdea: Split the screen between Seel wobbling on shore and gliding smoothly beneath icy water.
candidates.note: Well supported and easy to stage, but the clumsy-on-land/graceful-in-water contrast is a fairly familiar animal-Pokémon profile and offers limited new information.

rounds.request: None needed: icebreaker-snorkel is strong enough. A stronger alternative would need an equally specific survival mechanic or contradiction, supported by a surprising fact and a clear visual payoff.
